title: Annotatio V §.IV: Reformed impugn Oral’s Fundamentalitatem still more; Anti-Irenicum stretch §§XI–XXIII
pass_a_gloss: For the rest the Reformed, as they rightly impugn the Oral Eating of Christ’s body as to Truth, so still more as to the Fundamentalitatem affixed to it for the Christian faith. When I myself had also undertaken to do this very thing in my Irenic little Tract, and had diluted the reasons for the Fundamentalitatem of Oral Eating devised by the Author in a certain Anti-Irenic Writing, the Author strives with all force both to overturn my reasons and to vindicate his from the exceptions. What he has brought into the midst under this name in Paragraphs XI, XIII through XXIII inclusive, we mean to touch the more concisely for our Annotation’s narrower bars, the more firmly we are persuaded from what he has alleged that he wished not so much to dispute seriously as to instruct his Respondent by what pact it is not so very shameful sometimes to shout against even the clearest truth, or to wrap and cover the same with a veil of Contradiction, if ever that is noticed about to be of use to a Disputant from some older hypothesis received by him and his faith’s companions.
pass_b_english: The Reformed impugn Oral not only as to truth but still more as to the Fundamentalitatem hung on it for Christian faith.

Strimesius’s Irenic tract answered the Author’s Anti-Irenic reasons for that fundamentality (§§XI, XIII–XXIII); he now touches them concisely — reading the Author less as serious dispute than as coaching a Respondent how to shout down clear truth for an older hypothesis.
source_text: Cæterùm Reformati, sicuti Mand. corp. Christi Oralem, quà Veritatem, meritò impugnant, ita adhuc magis, quà affictam eidem fidei Christianæ Fundamentalitatem. Ipsum hoc cùm & ego in Tractatulo meo Irenico facere instituissem, rationes etiam pro Fundamentalitate Oralis Manducationis ab Autore, in Anti-Irenico quodam Scripto, excogitatas, diluissem, Autor & meas rationes evertere, & suas ab exceptionibus vindicare omni ope annititur. Ab eo, hoc nomine, Paragraphis XI. XIII. ad XXIII. inclusive, in medium adducta, pro angustioribus Annotationis nostræ cancellis, tantò concisiùs perstringere nobis animus est, quantò ex allatis ab eodem persuasi firmiùs sumus, non tàm disputare eum seriò, quàm Respondentem suum instruere voluisse, quô pactô veritati etiam clarissimæ quandoque obstrepere, quóve Contradictionis velô eandem involvere atque obducere haud adeo multùm verecundandum sit, si quando id ex usu hypotheseos cujusdam antiquioris, Disputanti, fideique suæ sociis receptæ, advertitur futurum.
